manifest.name: @askdkc/dsh-cli
manifest.description: Interactive terminal interface for DeepSeek Harness agents, sessions and tools.

scripts.build:dsh-auth: pnpm --dir dsh-auth install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts && pnpm --dir dsh-auth run build
scripts.compile: npm run build:dsh-std && npm run build:dsh-auth && npm run build:working-activity && npm run clean && tsc -p tsconfig.json
scripts.build: npm run compile && npm run verify:build
scripts.verify:build:inner: npm run verify:build-environment && npm run verify:boundary && npm run verify:contract && npm run verify:cli-startup-lifecycle && npm run verify:ignore-kiokuko && npm run verify:herdr && npm run verify:manifest-deps && npm run verify:pat...
scripts.verify:package: node scripts/verify-publish-manifest.mjs && node scripts/with-publish-manifest.mjs npm pack --dry-run --json --ignore-scripts | node scripts/verify-package.mjs
scripts.verify:approval-visibility: node --import tsx/esm scripts/verify-approval-visibility.tsx && npm run verify:approval-source-badge
scripts.verify:task-workflow: node scripts/verify-task-workflow.mjs && node scripts/verify-task-model-switch.mjs && node scripts/verify-channel-task-workflow.mjs

bundle.text:
# The dsh-cli bundle patch: the interactive terminal front door over the
# dsh-base layer. Applied after dsh-base's insert; rows here override base
# rows by id, with the profile's own cordis.patch.yml and any --patch
# overlays still to come.
#
# A patch replaces the targeted row's whole `config`, so each row below
# restates every key it owns (see the dsh-base patch for the shared
# defaults). The dsh-base core rows that need no dsh-cli value — tools,
# sandbox/approval policy, skills, goal, plan mode, workspace context,
# telemetry — are inherited unless this surface explicitly restates them.

# ── surface-specific values over the dsh-base layer ─────────────────────────

# Deployment persona, overridden by DSH_CLI_PERSONA.
- id: system-prompt
  config: !!js >-
    ({ personaPrefix: process.env.DSH_CLI_PERSONA ?? "You are a coding agent. Respond in the language of the user's request; use English when it is unclear. Do not infer the response language from instructions, quoted text, files, tool output, or the interface language." })

# The native DeepSeek adapter, pinned to the harness defaults: full thinking
# at max effort, key and base URL from the launching environment. The base
# entry supplies the adapter defaults; /settings edits the profile config
# through the current Loader service.
# apiKeyEnv names the credential environment variable.
- id: llm-deepseek
  config:
    apiKeyEnv: 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY'
    baseURL: !!js process.env.DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL
    thinking: enabled
    reasoningEffort: max

# The TUI creates (or resumes) its agent at runtime through the agent
# factory; no declarative agents are started at boot, and the configured
# agent list stays the base's empty default.
- id: agent-loop
  config:
    agents: []

# Preserve the TUI's opt-in privacy stance across the 0.1.2 base default
# change to FEEDBACK_ONLY. An explicit DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE still wins. This
# restates the whole 0.1.2 config because include patches replace config
# objects rather than merging them.
- id: session-telemetry-otel
  config:
    mode: !!js process.env.DSH_TELEMETRY_MODE || 'DISABLED'
    shutdownTimeoutMillis: 3000
    exporter:
      url: !!js process.env.DSH_TELEMETRY_OTLP_URL ?? 'https://harness-telemetry.deepseeksvc.com/v1/logs'
      compression: gzip
      timeoutMillis: 1000
    processor:
      scheduledDelayMillis: 10000
      maxQueueSize: 2048
      maxExportBatchSize: 2048
      exportTimeoutMillis: 1500

# The 0.1.2 base sends the active Loader package inventory on official
# DeepSeek requests by default. TUI keeps that diagnostic metadata opt-in.
- id: plugin-package-inventory-deepseek
  config:
    enabled: false

# ── agent presets (issue #8) ────────────────────────────────────────────────
#
# Presets own their tools and prompt sections. Disable equivalent host rows
# so isolated compositions such as minimal do not inherit extra tools.

- id: agent-instructions
  disabled: true

- id: command-compact
  disabled: true

# compaction lives in the preset's own isolate realm (standard/ptc/cordis
# carry `compaction-basic` with package defaults; minimal has none). The old
# ratio/retain tunables retired with this host row — preset compositions own
# their compaction config.
- id: compaction-basic
  disabled: true

- id: plan-mode
  disabled: true

- id: skill-filesystem
  disabled: true

- id: tool-bash
  disabled: true

- id: tool-fs
  disabled: true

- id: tool-fs-search
  disabled: true

- id: command-goal
  disabled: true

- id: tool-goal
  disabled: true

- id: tool-jobs
  disabled: true

- id: tool-pwsh
  disabled: true

- id: tool-result-pruner
  disabled: true

- id: tool-skill
  disabled: true

# `tool-str-replace-editor` carries no disable row: dsh-base registered that
# entry only up to the 0.1.2 line, and from 0.1.3-alpha.2 it is opt-in (see the
# dsh-base README). A row here would target a missing id and log
# `patch: entry "tool-str-replace-editor" not found` on every 0.1.3+ boot.
# Presets that expose the tool re-add the entry themselves.

# Delegation tools (subagent spawn/fork, controls, workflows) are preset rows
# now; the preset's `delegation` group re-adds them with package defaults, so
# the former TUI's depth-1 cap no longer applies.
- id: tool-subagent
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-control
  disabled: true

- id: tool-subagent-fork
  disabled: true

- id: tool-todo
  disabled: true

- id: tool-web
  disabled: true

- id: tool-workflow
  disabled: true

# Windows has no sandbox confinement backend yet (sandbox-local's win32
# chain is empty); use danger-full-access on Windows so bash commands can
# run. Other platforms keep the base workspace-write default.
- id: sandbox-policy
  config:
    mode: !!js "process.platform === 'win32' ? 'danger-full-access' : (process.env.DSH_PERMISSION_MODE ?? 'workspace-write')"
    workspaceRoot: !!js process.cwd()

# On Windows, skip approval prompts (no sandbox = the user's terminal trust
# model, matching every other terminal coding agent).
- id: approval
  config:
    policy: !!js "process.platform === 'win32' ? 'never' : ((process.env.DSH_PERMISSION_MODE ?? 'workspace-write') === 'danger-full-access' ? 'never' : 'ask')"

# Sessions live in the shared JSONL store (~/.dsh/sessions) — the same
# backend dsh web writes — so /resume here and the web session list see each
# other (#24). The row itself comes from the dsh-base layer; this override
# only re-points the root when DSH_CLI_SESSION_ROOT is set (test isolation).
- id: session-persistence-jsonl
  config:
    root: !!js process.env.DSH_CLI_SESSION_ROOT ?? dshHomePath('sessions')

# ── dsh-cli rows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# The `user-interaction` service row comes from the dsh-base bundle layer
# (mounted before this layer); do not insert it again — the include patch
# semantics would create a duplicate row. dsh-cli defensively creates the
# service on its own context when no composition provides it (bare
# `dsh --config cordis.yml` boots), then mounts the model-facing
# ask_user_question tool. On legacy hosts it registers the TUI provider on
# `ctx.userQuestions`; on Alpha it answers the scoped
# `user-questions/request` waterfall.

- insert:
    # Workspace grouping is a separate durable ledger, not a cwd-derived
    # projection. Mount the same domain stack and storage root as dsh-web-app
    # so TUI-created sessions can attach to the exact registry Web reads.
    #
    # These rows own host-plane services that the official web-app bundle may
    # already mount. Loader entry ids are process-global, so these
    # rows use dsh-cli-* scoped ids and self-disable when an enabled row with
    # the official id/name is already present in the tree. The disabled check
    # is evaluated during the same include update that inserts every row, so
    # it sees the web-app rows regardless of their activation state.
    - id: dsh-cli-storage
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'storage' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage' && !entry.disabled)"

    - id: dsh-cli-storage-json
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'storage-json' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-json' && !entry.disabled)"
      config:
        root: !!js dshHomePath('storages')

    - id: dsh-cli-storage-domain
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'storage-domain' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-storage-domain' && !entry.disabled)"
      config:
        backend: json

    # Scoped services yield to active official rows in mixed profiles.

    - id: dsh-cli-workspace
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'workspace' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-workspace' && !entry.disabled)"

    # Delegation settings yield to the official row in mixed profiles.
    - id: dsh-cli-subagent-model-selection-settings
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'subagent-model-selection-settings' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent/model-selection-settings' && !entry.disabled)"

    # Generic terminal workspace registry. Optional plugins add providers;
    # the TUI itself always supplies LOCAL and has no provider-specific code.
    - id: dsh-cli-workspaces
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/workspaces'

    # Optional plugins contribute nested slash-command completion here;
    # execution and durable command events remain owned by dsh-commands.
    - id: dsh-cli-command-trees
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/command-trees'
    # Optional plugins declare editable settings sections here (issue #165);
    # storage, validation and writes remain owned by the dsh settings service.
    - id: dsh-cli-settings-sections
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/settings-sections'

    # Optional plugins register full-screen scenes (trajectory-style whole-
    # terminal views) here and open them from their own command handlers;
    # rendering and input ownership remain owned by the TUI's Chat screen.
    - id: dsh-cli-scenes
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/scenes'

    # Plugin-interop anchor (Community Consensus v0.15): the unified grant
    # store, runtime generation id, and Host Descriptor live here; later
    # contract surfaces (plugin storage, message observation, effect
    # ledger) mount off THIS row's apply, so the patch surface changes only
    # once for the whole alignment. Mounted ahead of the extensions row and
    # any third-party plugin row.
    - id: dsh-cli-plugin-host
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/plugin-host'

    # Plugin-facing UI seams (the pi-style extension surface): managed
    # dialogs (select/confirm/input), keyed status-line contributions,
    # keyboard shortcuts, and custom session-entry text renderers. The
    # decision events (tui/input, tui/rewind-prompt, tui/session-switch,
    # tui/compact, …) are fired by the channel on the cordis bus directly
    # and need no row.
    - id: dsh-cli-extensions
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/extensions'

    # Current declarative registry. Web may already own this seat.
    - id: dsh-cli-agent-preset-registry
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'agent-preset-registry' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset-registry' && !entry.disabled)"
      config:
        default: standard

    # Host-plane services the `cordis` preset's plugin-experimentation tool
    # waits on (dynamicCordisRunner/cordisInspect); dsh-base carries no such
    # row — the official web app inserts it the same way, so this copy yields
    # to it when it is already present.
    - id: dsh-cli-cordis-host-runner
      name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-host-runner'
      disabled: !!js "[...ctx.loader.entries()].some(entry => entry.options.id === 'cordis-host-runner' && entry.options.name === '@deepseek-ai/dsh-cordis-host-runner' && !entry.disabled)"

    # Provider authentication (bundled dsh-auth dependency): mounts catalog
    # and custom provider routes plus the /auth command; the TUI's /provider
    # wizard gains its authentication branch from
    # the ctx.dshAuth service this row provides. Entry-level inject only —
    # the plugin module's own inject is empty so a stale patch cannot
    # deadlock a composition lacking these services (#183 pattern).
    - id: dsh-cli-auth
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/oauth'
      inject: [llm, commands]

    # The interactive front door. The plugin creates/resumes its agent at
    # runtime, seeds the startup status line, and disposes the whole app tree
    # (exiting the process) when the TUI unmounts. `dsh-cli --resume`
    # feeds the session id through DSH_CLI_RESUME_SESSION (see
    # src/sessionHistory.ts for the launcher contract).
    - id: dsh-cli
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli'
      # The entry-level dependency augments the plugin's `agents` inject and
      # prevents startup Session creation from racing WorkspaceRegistry init.
      inject: [workspaceRegistry, agents, tuiWorkspaces, tuiScenes, tuiDialogs, tuiStatus, tuiShortcuts, tuiRenderers, tuiThemes]
      # `tuiWorkspaces`/`tuiScenes` (and the dsh-cli-extensions services,
      # including `tuiThemes`)
      # live in the entry-level inject ONLY as an ordering (and reload-rebind)
      # guarantee alongside their service rows
      # above — they are deliberately absent from the plugin's code-level
      # inject (issue #183): the dsh CLI may read this patch from an older
      # copy of the package than the plugin module it loads, and a hard
      # code-level inject then deadlocks the tree at boot ("pending (waiting
      # for service: tuiWorkspaces)"). Without the rows the TUI degrades:
      # /workspace falls back to the local-only runtime, plugin scenes never
      # open. (The comment sits below the inject line:
      # verify-workspace-attachment.mjs asserts the name→inject distance.)
      config:
        provider: deepseek-official
        # Alt-screen fullscreen 布局：应用内鼠标选区（选择即复制, OSC 52 +
        # wl-copy/xclip/xsel 兜底）、滚轮滚动、双击选词/三击选行。出厂默认开启，
        # 与 schema 默认（index.ts fullscreen default true）保持一致——两处必须
        # 同步翻转，否则本覆盖层会盖住 schema 默认，更新后用户仍落在 inline。
        # 想退回 inline 主屏（终端原生滚动/选择）：/settings 全屏开关或 cordis.yml
        # `fullscreen: false`——显式选择始终优先于默认。
        fullscreen: true
        # 在支持的终端预览图片；/settings 可关闭，重启生效。
        terminalImages: true
        # Edit/Write diff 呈现：auto（≥110 列双栏对照，窄屏统一式）/
        # split（强制双栏）/ unified（强制统一式）。/settings 屏可实时改。
        # diffLayout: auto
        # 回复中的 ```mermaid 代码块画成字符图；false 保留源码。/settings 可实时改。
        # mermaidDiagrams: true
        # 每个请求实际生效的推理强度，按当前路由的 adapter 档位校验
        #（deepseek: off/low/high/max）；非法值回落 adapter 默认。
        effort: max
        # Shift+Tab session-mode cycle (array order IS the cycle order;
        # absent → the built-in default/plan/full trio below). Each entry
        # may declare any subset of the plan (on/off), sandbox (read-only/
        # workspace-write/danger-full-access), and approval (ask/never)
        # atoms; undeclared atoms are untouched. Entry index 0 is the
        # unmarked base mode.
        # modes:
        #   - id: default
        #     plan: false
        #     sandbox: workspace-write
        #     approval: ask
        #   - id: plan
        #     plan: true
        #     sandbox: read-only
        #     approval: ask
        #   - id: full
        #     plan: false
        #     sandbox: danger-full-access
        #     approval: never
        # Static preset choice (DSH_CLI_PRESET overrides): wins over the
        # persisted `/preset` preference (~/.dsh-cli/agent-preset.json), which
        # wins over the roster default (standard).
        preset: !!js process.env.DSH_CLI_PRESET ?? undefined
        workspace: !!js process.env.DSH_CLI_WORKSPACE_TARGET ?? undefined
        sessionId: !!js process.env.DSH_CLI_RESUME_SESSION ?? undefined

    # Live working-line data source (thinking copy / running tool / turn
    # summary). Mounted through dsh-cli's own
    # `./working-activity` re-export, NOT the bare `dsh-working-activity`
    # name: the dsh Loader resolves row names from the profile directory,
    # and pnpm's isolated node_modules layout never links a transitive
    # dependency into the profile root (npm's flat layout hid this), so the
    # bare name died with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND and disposed the whole app at
    # boot (#60).
    # The plugin stays mounted for its narration/system-prompt features and
    # publishes the `workingActivity` session projection, which is where the
    # TUI's working line comes from; never persist activity/status, so the
    # shared log remains Web-readable.
    - id: working-activity
      name: '@askdkc/dsh-cli/working-activity'
      config:
        lang: input
        publish: false
        publishIntervalMs: 500

readme.text: English | 简体中文 | 日本語

> An interactive terminal UI plugin for DeepSeek Harness.

This is dkc's independently developed fork of [dsh-TUI by chimney](https://github.com/ccch1mneyyy/dsh-TUI).

readme.section: Run without Kiokuko for one launch
readme.text:
```sh
dsh-cli --ignore-kiokuko
dsh-cli --ignore-kiokuko --resume <session-id>
```

readme.section: Run without Kiokuko for one launch
readme.text:
`dsh-cli` works independently; Kiokuko is optional. `--ignore-kiokuko` prevents
`kiokuko-dsh` and its subpath plugins (including model integration) from loading
for this launch, before their imports, services, tools or hooks run. It omits
Kiokuko's bundle effects while preserving explicit profile, home and `--patch`
overrides and other plugins. Kiokuko-provided providers/tools are unavailable.
Existing session history remains; resuming does not re-enable the plugin.

readme.section: Run without Kiokuko for one launch
readme.text:
The option does not uninstall anything or save an opt-out setting. Temporary
composition files are removed after use; the next launch without the flag uses
the ordinary profile again. It is a startup option, not an unload command for an
already-running session. `--dump-config` shows the effective startup tree;
schema/default-only dumps and profile replacement cannot be combined with this
option. If the host cannot safely compose the exclusion, startup fails with a
diagnostic rather than silently loading Kiokuko. Normal host startup housekeeping
and explicit in-session settings edits still follow the host's normal behavior.

- Streaming Markdown, tool cards, images, Mermaid diagrams, and keyboard completion.
- A pixel whale, live work status, context bar, TPS gauge, and clickable timeline.
- Session management with resume, fork, rewind, background work, and export.
- DSH presets, skills, MCP, goals, subagents, provider authentication, and extensions.
- Authentication for OpenAI, Claude, OpenCode, OpenRouter, Hermes Agent, and Infron.
- Virtualized rendering and bounded caches for long sessions.
- Optional scoped code analysis through the separate LSP provider; see
  [code-analysis setup and current acceptance limits](docs/code-intelligence.en.md).
- Optional Common Lisp mode through the separate `kiokuko-dsh` plugin, which
  must be installed in the same profile; see
  [Kiokuko Lisp setup](#optional-kiokuko-lisp-mode).

Requires [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) `>=22.19.0`, pnpm 11, a
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) source
checkout with dependencies installed, and `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`. We aim to support
current DSH APIs. Compatibility is checked against installed packages and the
upstream default branch, without a release allowlist; see [ADAPTER.md](ADAPTER.md).

Clone recursively to fetch submodules. In an existing checkout, run
`git submodule update --init --recursive` before installation.

```sh
git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/askdkc/dsh-cli.git
cd dsh-cli
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm build

Replace `~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness` with your checkout path. The first interactive
launch registers `dsh-cli`; open a new shell, then run it from your project directory.
The managed command saves the built Harness checkout path, so a separate global
DSH installation is unnecessary. Harness `plugin add` refreshes an existing managed
command during updates; no manual registration is needed. An explicit
`DSH_CLI_DSH_ROOT` overrides the saved path.
To update this fork, rebuild and reinstall the tarball. `/update` uses the registry.

Use the named `@askdkc/dsh-cli@file:...` form for local tarball updates. A bare
tarball path can fail with `ENOENT` when pnpm resolves a previous `file:` dependency
whose archive has been deleted. `TARBALL` holds the archive's absolute path; pass
it to the install command instead of executing it.

For PATH setup and install issues, see [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md).

Lisp mode is provided by the separate
[`kiokuko-dsh`](https://github.com/askdkc/kiokuko-dsh) plugin. dsh-cli supplies
the terminal prompt and `/kioku-lisp` command handling, but the plugin must be
installed in the same DSH profile:

```sh
cd ~/DIR/TO/deepseek-harness
pnpm dsh plugin --profile dsh-cli add kiokuko-dsh
```

Enable Lisp in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (by default
`~/.dsh/profiles/dsh-cli/cordis.patch.yml`), then restart `dsh-cli`:

```yaml
- id: kiokuko-dsh
  config:
    enabled: true
    lisp:

A working SBCL is required; Linux also needs Bubblewrap with user, PID, and
network namespaces. Profiles are isolated, so adding the plugin to another
profile, such as `web`, does not enable Lisp mode in `dsh-cli`. Without the
plugin, `/kioku-lisp` is unavailable and no Lisp-mode choice appears. With the
plugin enabled, startup waits for it, and activation that exceeds 30 seconds
stops startup with a diagnostic.

After restart, `/kioku-lisp status` reports whether Lisp is available. A coding
request can then offer the Lisp choice, or `/kioku-lisp enable` turns it on for
the session. See [Getting started](docs/getting-started.en.md#optional-kiokuko-lisp-workflow)
for consent, managed operations, and command timing.

`Enter` sends, `Tab` completes, `Ctrl+Enter` interrupts and sends, and double
`Esc` rewinds. Press `?` for shortcuts.

The working-status line follows each accepted request in English, Japanese, or
Chinese. Ambiguous short requests keep that session's previous progress language;
`/lang` controls the rest of the interface separately.

`/resume` opens the session manager; `/auth` connects providers and `/model`
selects a model. `/bg` keeps a session running until the TUI exits. See
[Interaction and commands](docs/interaction.en.md) for the full reference.

`/model` opens a centered picker with Favorites, Recent, and provider sections.
`/model seek deep` opens it with an order-independent search; an exact
`/model provider/model-id` switches directly. In the picker, use `Ctrl+F` to
toggle a favorite, `Ctrl+A` to connect a provider, and `Esc` to close.

To import Claude Code, Codex, OMP, zcode, or Grok Build conversations, run
`dsh-cli migrate` to see available histories, then
`dsh-cli migrate <agent> [--dry-run]`. Tool traffic is not imported.
See [Session migration](docs/migrate.en.md).
